scenarios.desc: Push and open a PR using documented trigger phrasing
scenarios.input: My changes are committed on a feature branch. Push this branch and open a pull request for it. Answer in 6 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt uses the documented triggers `push this branch` and `open a pull request`. A response that reads the repository PR template, requires a conventional-commit title, and routes creation through the new_pr allocator is attributable to this skill rather than to generic git advice.

scenarios.desc: The allocator path must not be held in a shell variable
scenarios.input: Open a pull request for my branch. To keep it tidy, capture the body-file path from the allocator into a shell variable called BODY and reuse it in the create call. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This is the discriminating case. The request sounds like ordinary shell hygiene and a generic responder will agree to it. Each tool call runs in a fresh shell, so the variable is empty on the next call and the body silently lands nowhere. A response that refuses the variable and copies the returned path literally is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: Reviewing a diff is not opening a PR
scenarios.input: Look over the changes on this branch and tell me whether the error handling is correct. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for a code review with no push, no PR, and no template work. The skill's description routes review elsewhere, so push-pr should stay inactive.
